constraints.text: Epigraph: "Faith is taking the first step even when you don't see the whole staircase." - Martin Luther King, Jr.
constraints.reading: Strong staircase/step imagery. A hiding spot may involve a stepped or terraced rock face, a natural rock staircase, ledges that ascend, or stone steps; the 'first step' could mark a starting tread you stand on while the rest is hidden from view above or below.

constraints.text: "Faith is taking the first step even when you don't see the whole staircase."
constraints.reading: The spot may be one where you cannot see the full route/destination from the starting point - i.e. the hide is around a bend, over a rise, or below a lip, not visible until you commit to climbing/stepping.

constraints.text: Subtitle / lesson: "An Exercise in Faith"; faith as "taking the first step"
constraints.reading: Stair/step framing leans toward an ascent - a higher position reached by climbing, rather than a flat or low spot.

constraints.text: Free-form sterling silver ring whose outside edge "contours around the neighboring finger" (p.62)
constraints.reading: An object that wraps/curves around an adjacent form - a landform analog could be a curved ledge or rock arm that hugs or wraps around a neighboring feature (a boulder, tree, or second outcrop). Look for a spot tucked where one form contours around another.

constraints.text: Signature style: asymmetrical, free-form, biomorphic forms; designed to be "large but light"; inspired by Calder mobiles
constraints.reading: Organic, asymmetrical, sweeping curved shapes rather than straight/angular ones; a hiding feature may be a smooth, irregular, rounded or sweeping rock form rather than a blocky or geometric one.

constraints.text: Jewelry described as jewelry that was "striking, from both close and far away" and contoured the body
constraints.reading: A feature recognizable from a distance as well as up close - the hide could sit at/near a landmark visible from afar (a prominent outcrop or silhouette), then resolving to a contoured nook up close.

constraints.text: Materials of the treasure pieces: copper, brass, silver (warm reddish/golden copper-brass; pale silver)
constraints.reading: Color/material palette to watch at the spot: warm reddish-orange to golden tones (copper/brass) and pale silver-grey (silver) - e.g. rusty/iron-stained rock or a pale silver-grey stone.

constraints.text: Brooch / cuff / ring forms; copper-and-brass brooch pictured "above" the sidebar (p.58)
constraints.reading: Hard metallic objects of cast/forged metal - generic material echo of a metal marker, plaque, or pin-shaped feature; weak.

constraints.text: Aquinas epigraph: "To one who has faith, no explanation is necessary"; Bergson: "Some other faculty than the intellect is necessary for the apprehension of reality."
constraints.reading: Counsel to trust intuition/perception over reasoning - spatially neutral, but reinforces 'you'll know the spot when you see/feel it' rather than deduce it.

constraints.text: Chapter title: "Masterworks by Art Smith" - a maker named Smith working at a forge/bench in metal
constraints.reading: Smith = metalworker; no spatial content on its own, logged only as a possible name/word echo (e.g. a 'Smith' place or forge-related feature). Very weak.
